title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. """Data loading for the proximity-kernel reproduction (claim C1: UCI Hepatitis).

Loads the classic UCI Hepatitis dataset (155 samples, 19 features + class),
converts UCI missing markers ('?') to NaN, and returns float arrays.

Paper reference: Table 2 (Hepatitis: 155 samples, 19 dim, 2 classes, 5.67%
missing) and Section 5.1 (all datasets from UCI, K-means with ground-truth K).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HEPATITIS_URLS = [
    "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
    "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/46/hepatitis.zip",
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bryan-0407/datasets/main/hepatitis.data",  # unused fallback
]

CACHE_FILE_CANDIDATES = [
    "hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
    "hepatitis.data",
    "uci_hepatitis.data",
    "uci/hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
]


def _download(url: str, dest: Path) -> None:
    import urllib.request

    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        data = resp.read()
    if url.endswith(".zip"):
        import io
        import zipfile

        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as zf:
            names = [n for n in zf.namelist() if n.endswith(".data") or n.endswith(".csv")]
            if not names:
                names = zf.namelist()
            dest.write_bytes(zf.read(names[0]))
    else:
        dest.write_bytes(data)


def load_hepatitis() -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return X (155x19 float, NaN for missing) and y (155 int in {0,1})."""
    cache = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    local_path: Path | None = None
    if cache:
        for rel in CACHE_FILE_CANDIDATES:
            p = Path(cache) / rel
            if p.exists() and p.is_file():
                local_path = p
                break
    if local_path is None:
        target = Path("data_cache/hepatitis.data")
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for url in HEPATITIS_URLS[:2]:
            try:
                _download(url, target)
                break
            except Exception:
                continue
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not download Hepatitis from any mirror")
        local_path = target

    df = pd.read_csv(local_path, header=None, na_values=["?", "", "NaN", "nan", "NA"])
    # Classic UCI Hepatitis: column 0 is the class (1=DIE, 2=LIVE), columns 1..19 features.
    y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).to_numpy()
    # map class to {0,1}
    classes = np.unique(y)
    assert len(classes) == 2, f"expected 2 classes, got {classes}"
    y = (y == classes[1]).astype(int)  # class 2 (LIVE) -> 1, class 1 (DIE) -> 0
    X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).to_numpy()

    assert X.shape == (155, 19), f"unexpected shape {X.shape}"
    assert y.shape == (155,)
    missing_frac = float(np.isnan(X).mean()) * 100.0
    assert 5.0 < missing_frac < 6.5, f"missing fraction {missing_frac:.2f}% does not match Table 2 (5.67%)"
    return X, y

"""Proximity kernel reimplementation from the paper (arXiv:2510.13352).

Pipeline (paper Section 4):
  4.1.1 Eq.(4):  per-feature bin centers = evenly-spaced percentiles of the
                 observed values, c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs_j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)),
                 k = 1..nbins  ->  centers include min and max.
  4.1.2 Eq.(5):  proximity assignment: each observed value -> nearest bin center.
  4.1.3 Eq.(6-7): one-hot encoding per feature, concatenated across features.
  4.2  Eqs.(8-14): three-level cascading fallback for missing values:
                 (1) intersection matching on all observed features (KME mean of
                     matching samples' one-hots for the missing feature),
                 (2) union matching on any observed feature,
                 (3) global bin-frequency prior.
  4.3  Eq.(15): K(xm, xn) = (1/d) * z_m^T z_n.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np


@dataclass
class FallbackDiagnostics:
    n_missing_entries: int = 0
    level1_entries: int = 0
    level2_entries: int = 0
    level3_entries: int = 0
    empty_S1_samples: int = 0  # samples whose intersection set S1(i) was empty
    empty_S2_samples: int = 0  # samples whose union set S2(i) was empty
    detail: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def fit_bins(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> tuple[list[np.ndarray | None], np.ndarray]:
    """Eq.(4): equal-frequency bin centers per feature (observed values only).

    Returns (centers_per_feature, global_prior) where global_prior[j] is the
    Eq.(13) bin-frequency distribution for feature j (uniform if all missing).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    centers_per_feature: list[np.ndarray | None] = []
    prior = np.full((d, nbins), 1.0 / nbins)
    pct = np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, nbins)  # (k-1)*100/(nbins-1), k=1..nbins
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers_per_feature.append(None)
            continue
        centers = np.percentile(obs, pct, method="linear")
        centers = np.asarray(centers, dtype=float)
        # degenerate features (all equal observed values): spread centers tiny bit
        if not np.all(np.diff(centers) > 0):
            lo = centers[0]
            centers = lo + np.arange(nbins) * 1e-9
        centers_per_feature.append(centers)
        b = np.argmin(np.abs(obs[:, None] - centers[None, :]), axis=1)
        prior[j] = np.bincount(b, minlength=nbins) / obs.size
    return centers_per_feature, prior


def assign_bins(X: np.ndarray, centers_per_feature: list[np.ndarray | None]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq.(5): proximity assignment of observed values to nearest center.

    Returns B (n, d) int; -1 for missing entries. Ties break to lowest index.
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        centers = centers_per_feature[j]
        if centers is None:
            continue
        obs_mask = ~np.isnan(X[:, j])
        vals = X[obs_mask, j]
        B[obs_mask, j] = np.argmin(np.abs(vals[:, None] - centers[None, :]), axis=1)
    return B


def encode_observed(B: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq.(6): one-hot encoding for observed entries. H[i, j] in {0,1}^nbins."""
    n, d = B.shape
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    for j in range(d):
        obs = B[:, j] >= 0
        H[obs, j, B[obs, j]] = 1.0
    return H


def compute_fallback_encodings(
    B: np.ndarray, H_obs: np.ndarray, prior: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, FallbackDiagnostics]:
    """Section 4.2: cascading fallback (intersection -> union -> global prior).

    For a missing entry (i, j) the KME average (Eqs. 10/12) is restricted to
    matching samples that have feature j observed (assumption A8), using their
    observed one-hot encodings. Falls back per-entry to the next level when the
    stricter level finds no eligible samples.
    """
    n, d, nbins = H_obs.shape
    H = H_obs.copy()
    missing_mask = B < 0
    diag = FallbackDiagnostics(n_missing_entries=int(missing_mask.sum()))
    samples_with_missing = np.where(missing_mask.any(axis=1))[0]
    for i in samples_with_missing:
        O_i = np.where(~missing_mask[i])[0]
        # C_{i,l}: samples m != i assigned to the same bin as i on feature l.
        if O_i.size > 0:
            eq = np.stack([B[:, l] == B[i, l] for l in O_i], axis=1)  # (n, |O_i|)
            eq[i, :] = False
            match_all = eq.all(axis=1)   # S1(i), Eq.(9)
            match_any = eq.any(axis=1)   # S2(i), Eq.(11)
        else:
            match_all = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
            match_all[i] = False
            match_any = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
        if not match_all.any():
            diag.empty_S1_samples += 1
        if not match_any.any():
            diag.empty_S2_samples += 1
        for j in np.where(missing_mask[i])[0]:
            obs_j = ~missing_mask[:, j]
            s1 = match_all & obs_j
            if s1.any():  # Level 1, Eq.(10)
                H[i, j] = H_obs[s1, j].mean(axis=0)
                diag.level1_entries += 1
                continue
            s2 = match_any & obs_j
            if s2.any():  # Level 2, Eq.(12)
                H[i, j] = H_obs[s2, j].mean(axis=0)
                diag.level2_entries += 1
                continue
            H[i, j] = prior[j]  # Level 3, Eq.(14)
            diag.level3_entries += 1
    diag.detail = {
        "missing_entries_per_feature": missing_mask.sum(axis=0).tolist(),
    }
    return H, diag


def build_representation(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, FallbackDiagnostics, np.ndarray]:

def evaluate_representation(

) -> dict:

    arr = np.asarray(nmis)
    return {

audit_summary: C1 is reproduced on the correct Hepatitis dataset (155x19, 167 missing entries) using full-dataset transductive K-means with K=2 and NMI, exactly matching the paper's evaluation protocol. The code implements the proximity kernel pipeline: observed-only percentile bin centers, nearest-center assignment, one-hot encoding, three-level cascading fallback, and K=(1/d)ZZ^T; the nbins grid is searched and nbins=2 gives mean NMI 0.228909 versus target 0.2289. The target value appears in code only as a pass/fail constant and is not used to compute the result, so the reported number is not hard-coded or echoed. C2-C8 aggregate and baseline claims were not attempted, but that is outside the C1 match target and does not make this a wrong experiment. requirement_check.evidence: src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins computes per-feature centers from observed values only using np.percentile; missing entries are not used in the percentile computation.
fit_bins uses np.linspace(0, 100, nbins) with method='linear', i.e. evenly spaced percentile centers including the feature min and max.
assign_bins assigns each observed value via np.argmin(np.abs(vals[:,None]-centers[None,:]), axis=1), giving nearest-center Voronoi assignment with deterministic lowest-index tie-breaking.
encode_observed creates one-hot H[i,j,bin] for observed entries, and build_representation reshapes H to Z with shape (n, d*nbins).
compute_fallback_encodings implements the three levels in order: intersection match S1, union match S2, then global prior.
Level 1 uses H_obs[s1,j].mean(axis=0) where s1 = S1(i) restricted to samples with feature j observed, matching assumption A8's well-defined KME reading.
Level 2 uses s2 = match_any & obs_j and averages H_obs[s2,j], implementing union matching when S1 fails.
Level 3 assigns prior[j], built from observed bin frequencies per feature; on Hepatitis the clean run shows level3=0, so the path is implemented but not triggered.
proximity_kernel/build_representation computes K=(Z@Z.T)/d. Clustering is run on Z; for a linear kernel this is equivalent to kernel K-means using K, so the similarity definition is not bypassed.
src/cluster.py runs sklearn KMeans with n_clusters=N_CLUSTERS=2 and computes normalized_mutual_info_score against y.
evaluate_representation runs seeds 0-9 and reports mean NMI; at selected nbins=2 all 10 seeds give identical NMI.
search_nbins evaluates the full grid [2,3,4,6,8] and selects the highest mean NMI; selected nbins=2 is logged in results/metrics.json.

No timing-scaling experiment is reported, and the fallback implementation loops over all n samples for each sample with missing values, giving O(n^2 d) worst-case pairwise matching rather than the paper's claimed linear-in-n matching.
encode_observed places a single 1 per observed feature; thus a complete sample has exactly d ones in d*nbins entries.
